item.title: Week 1: Fundamentals of AI
item.description:
Week 1: Fundamentals of AI

Focus: What is AI/ML? Brief history and overview

📚 Required Readings

Primary Readings

  1. “Artificial Intelligence: A Brief History” (15 min read)

    • Overview of AI development from symbolic AI to modern machine learning
    • Key figures and pivotal moments in AI research

  2. “What is Machine Learning?” (20 min read)

    • Difference between AI and machine learning
    • Supervised vs. unsupervised learning basics
    • Real-world examples of ML applications

Supplementary Resources

  • Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Artificial Intelligence (link) — Philosophical foundations
  • “A Very Short Introduction to Artificial Intelligence” — Excerpts (10 min)

💭 Discussion Prompts

Before class, consider these questions as you read:

item.title: Week 2: AI Systems & Data
item.description:
Week 2: AI Systems & Data

Focus: How AI systems work; data and training

📚 Required Readings

Primary Readings

  1. “How Machine Learning Works: The Training Process” (25 min)

    • Training data, features, and labels
    • Algorithms and parameter optimization
    • Testing and validation

  2. “Data: The Fuel of AI” (20 min)

    • Data collection and preparation
    • Data quality and representation
    • The role of big data in modern AI

Supplementary Resources

  • “The Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems” — Selected sections
  • Interactive visualizations: Neural network playground

💭 Discussion Prompts

  1. Why is data quality more important than data quantity?
  2. How do training decisions affect AI system behavior in the real world?
  3. What role does feedback play in AI systems over time?

📝 Preparation for Class

  • Find a dataset related to a topic you care about (e.g., Kaggle, UCI Machine Learning Repository)
  • Reflect on what patterns you’d hope an AI system would find in that data
  • Consider: What could go wrong if the data was biased or incomplete?

🔗 Related Assignment

See Week 2 Assignment for this week’s task.

item.title: Week 3: Ethics & Bias
item.description:
Week 3: Ethics & Bias

Focus: Algorithmic bias and fairness

📚 Required Readings

Primary Readings

  1. “Weapons of Math Destruction” — Chapter 1 (30 min)

    • How algorithms can amplify inequality
    • Case studies of biased AI systems
    • The impact on vulnerable communities

  2. “Defining and Detecting Algorithmic Bias” (25 min)

    • Statistical definitions of fairness
    • Types of bias: historical, measurement, representation, evaluation
    • Methods for detecting and mitigating bias

Supplementary Resources

  • ProPublica: “Machine Bias” investigation — Interactive article
  • “The Ethics of Artificial Intelligence” — Stanford Encyclopedia excerpt

💭 Discussion Prompts

  1. How can an AI system be mathematically “accurate” yet fundamentally unfair?
  2. When is some level of bias acceptable in AI systems?
  3. Who should be responsible for the harms caused by biased algorithms?

📝 Preparation for Class

  • Read about a real-world case of algorithmic bias (e.g., Amazon hiring, COMPAS, facial recognition)
  • Prepare a 2-minute summary: What went wrong? Who was harmed?
  • Brainstorm: How could that system have been designed more fairly?

🔗 Related Assignment

See Week 3 Assignment for this week’s task.

item.title: Week 4: Policy & Governance
item.description:
Week 4: Policy & Governance

Focus: Regulation and policy approaches

📚 Required Readings

Primary Readings

  1. “Global AI Governance Approaches” (30 min)

    • EU AI Act overview
    • US regulatory landscape
    • Approaches from China, Canada, and other regions
    • Key principles: transparency, accountability, human control

  2. “Regulating AI: The Challenge of Speed and Change” (25 min)

    • Why traditional regulation struggles with AI
    • Policy options: principles-based vs. rules-based regulation
    • Role of self-regulation, industry standards, and technical safety

Supplementary Resources

  • Summary of the EU AI Act
  • NIST AI Risk Management Framework overview
  • Stanford AI Index 2024 — Policy section

💭 Discussion Prompts

  1. What are the tradeoffs between innovation and regulation?
  2. Should AI regulation be global or local? Why?
  3. How can policymakers stay informed about rapidly evolving technology?

📝 Preparation for Class

  • Choose one recent AI policy or regulation (EU AI Act, Biden Executive Order, etc.)
  • Prepare a 2-minute summary: What does it do? What problems does it aim to solve?
  • Consider: Is this approach effective? What are its limitations?

🔗 Related Assignment

See Week 4 Assignment for this week’s task.

item.title: Week 5: Employment & Economics
item.description:
Week 5: Employment & Economics

Focus: Job displacement, economic implications

📚 Required Readings

Primary Readings

  1. “AI and the Future of Work” (30 min)

    • Historical context: previous waves of technological disruption
    • Which jobs are most vulnerable to automation?
    • Retraining and reskilling: what has worked before?

  2. “Economic Inequality and AI” (25 min)

    • Winner-take-all dynamics in AI markets
    • Wealth concentration and market power
    • Policy responses: UBI, wage subsidies, taxation approaches

Supplementary Resources

  • McKinsey: “The Future of Work After COVID-19” — Selected sections
  • “Race After Technology” by Ruha Benjamin — Chapter on economics

💭 Discussion Prompts

  1. What economic sectors are most at risk from AI automation in the next 10 years?
  2. How might society distribute the economic gains from AI productivity?
  3. Is job displacement from AI different from job loss from other technologies? How?

📝 Preparation for Class

  • Research one occupation you’re interested in: How might AI change that field?
  • Find 2-3 policy proposals addressing AI and employment
  • Reflect: Which approach(es) seem most promising to you? Why?

🔗 Related Assignment

See Week 5 Assignment for this week’s task.

item.title: Week 6: AI in Society
item.description:
Week 6: AI in Society

Focus: Applications across domains

📚 Required Readings

Primary Readings

  1. “AI in Healthcare: Promises and Pitfalls” (25 min)

    • Diagnostic AI systems
    • Drug discovery and personalized medicine
    • Equity in healthcare AI applications

  2. “AI in Criminal Justice: Beyond Predictive Policing” (25 min)

    • Risk assessment algorithms in sentencing
    • Bias in criminal justice AI systems
    • Transparency and accountability challenges

Supplementary Resources

  • “AI in Education: Opportunities and Risks” — Brief overview
  • Case studies from your field of interest

💭 Discussion Prompts

  1. What are the unique ethical considerations in high-stakes domains like healthcare or criminal justice?
  2. How do we balance innovation benefits with preventing harm?
  3. Who should benefit most from AI applications?

📝 Preparation for Class

  • Choose one domain where AI is being deployed (healthcare, education, transportation, finance, etc.)
  • Research: What does the AI system do? What problem does it solve?
  • Analyze: What are the potential benefits and harms for different groups?

🔗 Related Assignment

See Week 6 Assignment for this week’s task.

item.title: Week 7: Midterm Review & Synthesis
item.description:
Week 7: Midterm Review & Synthesis

Focus: Integration of Weeks 1-6 concepts

📚 Review Readings

Key Concepts to Review

  1. AI Fundamentals (Weeks 1-2)

    • What is AI/ML? How systems are trained.
    • Key terminology and basic processes

  2. Ethics and Governance (Weeks 3-4)

    • Bias and fairness definitions
    • Policy approaches and regulatory frameworks

  3. Societal Impact (Weeks 5-6)

    • Economic implications and employment
    • Domain-specific applications

Study Materials

  • Glossary of key terms
  • Summary charts and timelines
  • Review questions from previous weeks

💭 Reflection Questions

  1. How have your views on AI and society evolved over the past 6 weeks?
  2. What are the most important ethical challenges we face?
  3. How do technical, policy, and societal factors interconnect?

📝 Midterm Preparation

  • Review all weekly reading discussion prompts
  • Revisit case studies from weeks 1-6
  • Prepare examples to illustrate key concepts
  • Formulate your own perspective on AI and society issues

🔗 Related Assessment

See Midterm Assessment for details on the midterm exam format and expectations.

item.description:

item.title: Week 9: Emerging Issues
item.description:
Week 9: Emerging Issues

Focus: Privacy, surveillance, generative AI

📚 Required Readings

Primary Readings

  1. “Privacy in the Age of AI” (25 min)

    • Data collection and personal privacy
    • Differential privacy and technical solutions
    • Right to privacy in different jurisdictions

  2. “Surveillance Capitalism” — Chapter selections (25 min)

    • Business models based on data extraction
    • Power asymmetries between individuals and platforms
    • Societal implications

  3. “Generative AI: Opportunities and Risks” (25 min)

    • How large language models work
    • Applications and capabilities
    • Concerns: bias, misinformation, environmental costs, training data ethics

Supplementary Resources

  • Facial recognition and mass surveillance — Current articles
  • Copyright and AI training data — Legal perspectives
  • “The Environmental Costs of AI” — Brief overview

💭 Discussion Prompts

  1. Is privacy still possible in a world of ubiquitous data collection?
  2. What responsibility do generative AI creators have for training data and outputs?
  3. How should we balance innovation in AI with protection of fundamental rights?

📝 Preparation for Class

  • Reflect on your own digital privacy: What data about you exists? Who has access?
  • Try a generative AI tool (ChatGPT, Claude, etc.): What can it do? What are its limitations?
  • Research one recent AI privacy or surveillance controversy

🔗 Related Assignment

See Week 9 Assignment for this week’s task.

item.title: Week 10: Autonomous Systems
item.description:
Week 10: Autonomous Systems

Focus: Self-driving cars, robotics, accountability

📚 Required Readings

Primary Readings

  1. “The Ethics of Autonomous Vehicles” (30 min)

    • How self-driving cars work (sensors, decision-making)
    • The trolley problem and real-world tradeoffs
    • Liability and insurance in autonomous systems
    • Safety standards and testing protocols

  2. “Robots in Society: Accountability and Control” (25 min)

    • Where are robots deployed? What tasks?
    • Human-robot interaction and trust
    • Who is responsible when autonomous systems cause harm?

Supplementary Resources

  • Tesla autopilot incidents and investigations
  • Boston Dynamics robots — Current capabilities and concerns
  • “Why Accountability Matters for Autonomous Weapons” — Brief overview

💭 Discussion Prompts

  1. Who should be held liable when an autonomous vehicle causes an accident?
  2. How much human oversight is necessary for autonomous systems?
  3. Should there be limits on where robots or autonomous systems can be deployed?

📝 Preparation for Class

  • Research one autonomous system currently in use (self-driving car, delivery robot, medical robot, etc.)
  • Prepare: How it works, current limitations, real-world incidents if any
  • Consider: What could go wrong? What safeguards exist?

🔗 Related Assignment

See Week 10 Assignment for this week’s task.

item.title: Week 11: Futures & Regulation
item.description:
Week 11: Futures & Regulation

Focus: Possible futures, values, and comprehensive regulation

📚 Required Readings

Primary Readings

  1. “The Future of AI: Scenarios and Possibilities” (30 min)

    • Optimistic scenarios: abundance, solutions to major challenges
    • Pessimistic scenarios: misalignment, power concentration
    • Most likely path: continued uncertainty and mixed outcomes
    • Role of decisions we make today

  2. “Comprehensive AI Governance Frameworks” (30 min)

    • Integration of technical, policy, and ethical approaches
    • Role of stakeholders: governments, industry, civil society, academia
    • International cooperation challenges
    • Building values into AI systems from the start

Supplementary Resources

  • AI policy recommendations from diverse organizations
  • “The Alignment Problem” — Overview of AI safety research
  • Scenarios from AI foresight exercises

💭 Discussion Prompts

  1. What future for AI and society would you most want to see?
  2. How can we ensure AI benefits are broadly shared?
  3. What values should guide AI development and deployment?

📝 Preparation for Class

  • Envision your preferred future with AI (5-10 years from now): What works well? What problems have been solved or prevented?
  • Write down 2-3 actions or policies that would help achieve that future
  • Reflect on obstacles and resistance that might prevent that future

🔗 Related Assignment

See Week 11 Assignment for this week’s task.
